correctness.rationale: Direct finite-dimensional proof via the nonzero spectra of the weighted projection and its 2x2 Gram matrix gives an exact identity for every normal. The positive lower-right minor makes the determinant event exactly equivalent to the CDF inequality. Gaussian-normal representation verifies the Dirichlet law and the coupled almost-sure rank-two limit; the limiting determinant is c2^{-2} G1^2 >0 almost surely, including an infinite leading-axis limit. An exact conditional normal tail formula and dominated convergence prove the positive t^{-1} constant and the iff p<1 moment threshold. Bounded truncations and weak convergence force E[R_N/sqrt(N)] to diverge in the supercritical regime. Full-hyperplane Jacobi reduction matches the 2x2 identity on 420 independent configurations to <1.1e-13. Limit statements are proved, not inferred from checks.

value.rationale: The first genuinely unequal two-spike family has a complete, shape-explicit one-measurement random-radius law, while best codimension-one information has radius equal to the second axis. The critical square-root-dimension matrix limit gives exact random-versus-optimal performance beyond order bounds, and the supercritical regime has an unbounded limiting law with a sharp inverse-linear tail and a phase change to infinite mean and divergence of the finite-dimensional expected random-to-optimal ratio. These are motivated structural statistics for the random-section and information-recovery problem, not arbitrary finite recomputations.
